title: 1952 Grade 9 orientation week
description: At Hartland High School, incoming Grade 9 students were required to participate in a week-long initiation; no exceptions. For years, new students could be seen around town dressed up in makeshift costumes. Photographs document this tradition from 1947 to 1955. The initiates had to follow the orders of older students and always let them go first. The activities were orderly and meant to be fun, ensuring that no one took offense. Each day brought a new challenge; one day, you might have to measure the bridge with straight pins while crawling on your hands and knees, or scrub the floor with a toothbrush. This picture, taken in 1952, shows (from left to right): Cheryl McMullin, Betty Stephenson, Rosemarie Carey, Evangeline Sherwood (looking over her shoulder), Eileen Clark, Laura Crabbe, and an unknown girl at the end.
